# Probot

> ESP32 Arduino library for educational robotics competitions (Turkish
> Ministry of Education / MEB). The robot hosts a WiFi access point and a
> browser-based driver station; joystick input streams to the robot over a
> binary WebSocket at 50 Hz. Library name in the Arduino Library Manager:
> "probot". Repository: https://github.com/probot-studio/probot-core
> Library version: 0.4.0

Rules that generated code MUST follow:

- Never define `setup()` or `loop()` — the library defines them.
- Lifecycle is the same FTC OpMode model: select Autonomous/TeleOp, then
  INIT, START, STOP. Use the main `autonomousInit/Loop/Stop` and
  `teleopInit/Loop/Stop` triples. The two loop and two stop hooks are required
  (missing = linker error); init is optional with an empty weak default.
- Advanced optional hooks: `autonomousInitLoop`/`teleopInitLoop` run between
  INIT and START with neutral input; `autonomousStart`/`teleopStart` run once
  at START. Do not put these in beginner examples unless their purpose is
  needed.
- Optional third mode for setup/maintenance code (calibration, homing):
  `utilityInit/InitLoop/Start/Loop/Stop`. The DS offers Utility only when
  `utilityLoop()` is defined. It has no timer. Use it only when asked.
- Define `PROBOT_WIFI_AP_SSID`, `PROBOT_WIFI_AP_PASSWORD` (min 8 chars)
  and `PROBOT_WIFI_AP_CHANNEL` (1-13) BEFORE `#include <probot.h>`. For
  a fleet, give each robot a distinct fixed channel by hand. Boot-time
  auto channel select is opt-in via `PROBOT_WIFI_AUTO_CHANNEL 1`
  (default off; single-robot use, not recommended for a fleet).
- Joystick access: `auto js = probot::io::joystick_api::makeDefault();`
  then `js.getLeftY()`, `js.getA()`, `js.getPOV()` etc. Axis range is
  -1..+1, Y is positive up. `probot::io::gamepad()` is the low-level
  service and has NO getLeftX/getA-style methods. A second driver's
  gamepad: `probot::io::joystick_api::makeForPort(1)` (ports 0-5).
- Servos: the library provides NO servo class — drive raw LEDC. In
  the relevant OpMode init call `ledcAttachChannel(pin, 50, 14, 7)` (a HIGH channel, so it
  never shares a timer with `analogWrite` motor PWM → no jitter); in the loop
  `ledcWrite(pin, us * 16383 / 20000)` for a 500-2500 us pulse. Not ESP32Servo,
  not analogWrite (1 kHz can't make a 50 Hz servo frame).
- initLoop/loop hooks are called at a fixed rate (default 20 ms, ~50 Hz;
  `probot::setLoopPeriodMs(ms)` changes it); do not write infinite loops or
  block longer than 2 s inside them, and do not call `delay()` in them
  (the library already waits between passes).
- Telemetry to the driver station panel: `probot::printf("v=%.2f\n", v);`
  (a screen the sketch may clear each loop). Messages that must stay
  (warnings, errors, events) go to the console:
  `probot::console::warning("battery %.1f V", v);` (`info`, `error` too),
  shown on the Logs page. Do not write to the console every loop.
- Extra .cpp files include `<probot/api.hpp>` (config-free), never
  `<probot.h>`, which belongs to the sketch only.
- To stop the running OpMode from code (for example on a fatal error),
  call `probot::requestStop()`: the same cooperative stop as the Driver
  Station STOP button. `probot::emergencyStop()` is terminal until reboot.
- Inputs auto-zero 500 ms after the link drops — driving motors directly
  from axis values is safe.
- Battery gauge in the UI: EITHER a voltage divider on an ADC1 pin
  (`PROBOT_BATTERY_ADC_PIN` 1-10 only — ADC2 pins 11-20 do not work with
  WiFi on — plus `PROBOT_BATTERY_R_TOP_K`/`_R_BOT_K` in kΩ), OR an I2C
  sensor (`PROBOT_BATTERY_INA 219` or `226`), never both. Without either,
  feed it manually with `probot::setBatteryVoltage(v)` or the UI shows
  "Veri yok". INA current: `probot::io::battery::currentAmps()` (NaN
  without an INA sensor). Low battery: `probot::io::battery::setLowVoltage(v)`
  sets the threshold (off by default), `isLowVoltage()` reads the flag.

## Docs

- [API reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/probot-studio/probot-core/stable/API.md): complete API, lifecycle, HTTP/WS protocol
- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/probot-studio/probot-core/stable/README.md): install, configuration macros, competition channel planning, servo jitter guide

## Examples

- [JoystickTest](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/probot-studio/probot-core/stable/examples/JoystickTest/JoystickTest.ino): read axes/buttons, print telemetry
- [TankDrive](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/probot-studio/probot-core/stable/examples/TankDrive/TankDrive.ino): two-motor drive with an H-bridge (BTS7960-style)
- [ServoTest](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/probot-studio/probot-core/stable/examples/ServoTest/ServoTest.ino): jitter-free servo control from the joystick
